M7.note: w2 ran three dsfw variants (dsfw, dsfw_fast, dsfw_mean); the lead reports the best. Under a no-effect null a given variant wins 3/3 at E64 with p=1/8, so at least one of three does with p=0.33. The E8 edge is strong (paired t=-9.3) but E64 (t=-2.55, p=0.13, df 2) is weak; R1/R2 treat 3/3 as sufficient, which the 1/8 null rate does not support at E64. Seed 4 (CPU) adds a 4th paired win at both E: E8 -1.38%, E64 -3.70%; 4-seed paired t E8 -12.8 (p=0.001), E64 -3.3 (p=0.047), df 3; sign test 4/4 p=0.0625 per E. So the bce_all edge replicates; the post-shift cost also replicates (+0.056 / +0.077). The false flag still rests on the lead's cost and family-label reasons, not on the edge being noise.

M6.stress_pass: M6.md stress pass (12:01Z merge) drops cg and fb01 under independent evidence; survivors across stress are b, cq, fb05 (M6/lead/M6-stress-verdict.json).
M6.note: The cg survival margin is ~0.0014 nats of noise excess (0.2% of ln 2) but consistent (paired t=-9.8, 3/3). The +35-44% learnable-BCE gap of cg vs (a) is LFSR16: (a) learnt it in 3/3 seeds, cg in 0/3 (Fisher one-sided p=0.050). Excluding LFSR16 cg ties BOOST. So cg survives on a tiny but real noise margin, and it systematically blocks LFSR16 learning in this harness; calling that seed luck is not supported by 3/3 vs 0/3. Seed 4: cg LFSR16 BCE 0.695 (not learnt; 0/4), BOOST 0.336 (learnt); cg noise still below BOOST (margin -0.0022).
